questions.q: How do distributed systems typically detect that a node has failed?
options: By directly inspecting the node's hardware remotely
Through heartbeats and timeouts — if no heartbeat arrives within a timeout window, the node is treated as failed
Failed nodes announce their own failure before going down
By polling a central authority that always knows the true state of every node
questions.explain: Failure detection is inference-based: missing heartbeats within a timeout window lead the rest of the cluster to treat a node as failed, even though this could be a false positive.

options: A failure that is immediately and completely contained with no further effects
A failure where one slow or failed dependency causes callers to pile up and exhaust their own resources, spreading the problem to otherwise-healthy services
A type of heartbeat message
A failure that only affects the leader node and never the followers
questions.explain: Cascading failure occurs when resource exhaustion from waiting on one failing dependency spreads outward, degrading services that had nothing originally wrong with them.

questions.q: What does a circuit breaker do that a simple timeout does not?
options: It permanently disables the dependency with no recovery path
After enough recent failures, it stops sending requests to the dependency entirely for a cooldown period, failing fast instead of letting calls pile up
It guarantees the dependency will never fail again
It removes the need for any timeout at all
questions.explain: A circuit breaker proactively stops traffic to a failing dependency during a cooldown, preventing the pileup of waiting calls that leads to cascading failure — beyond what a per-call timeout alone does.

questions.q: In Raft-style leader election, what triggers a follower to become a candidate?
options: A manual command from a system administrator
Its election timer expires with no heartbeat received from the current leader
It receives a vote request from every other node simultaneously
The cluster's clock reaches a globally agreed time
questions.explain: A follower suspects the leader has failed when its election timer expires without a heartbeat, prompting it to become a candidate and request votes.

questions.q: Why does requiring a MAJORITY vote to elect a new leader prevent "split brain" (two leaders at once)?
options: Because majorities are always unanimous
Because two different candidates cannot both receive a majority of votes from the same fixed set of voters at the same time
Because split brain is prevented by using faster hardware
Because majority voting eliminates the need for heartbeats
questions.explain: Since more than half of a fixed voter set can't be split between two different candidates simultaneously, requiring a majority mathematically guarantees at most one leader can win per term.
